title: Normalized geometric boundary models from the site comparisons
statement: Fix the finite-field datum D of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime l distinct from its characteristic p, a finite extension E of Q_l, n a natural number, and a separated finite-type scheme Y over D.k. At coefficient level A=O_E/(varpi_E^(n+1)), for every locally closed piece of Y and every closed boundary arrow, there exists one system of the canonical operations of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input] satisfying their literal site-coordinate normalizations and admitting the normalized geometric model of [def-weil-boundary-normalized-model]. In particular this statement asks for no boundary-exchange invertibility and no boundary-exchange double-dual compatibility.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-boundary-finite-tor-domains] at level n+1 to every immersion into Y. Obtain separated finite-type pieces, preservation by ordinary and exceptional etale restrictions, etale dual preservation and invertible delta. The constant coefficient ring is finite and has invertible exponent since l differs from the characteristic.

Take all operation fields literally from [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]. Use [lem-weil-duality-pairing] to normalize symmetry and evaluation. Apply [thm-fix-general-biduality] and the evaluation-compatible internal-Hom comparison to obtain preservation and native delta invertibility in the fixed comparison dualizing object.

Apply [lem-weil-boundary-evaluation-currying] with the finite-Tor domains and projection formula [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] to construct q and prove naturality. Apply [lem-weil-boundary-alpha-normalization] to the same q and admissible domains to obtain invertibility of this particular alpha, rather than choosing an existence-only costalk isomorphism.

Use [lem-weil-boundary-finite-site-realization] to identify q, evaluation, dualizing objects and biduality on every finite-Tor etale-origin object with the pro-etale constructions. In comparison-pullback dualizing coordinates define theta as inverse C_ZG(unit) followed by C_Z(ecomp), and tau as inverse s(counit) tensor identity followed by tensorModel. Thus their normalization equations hold. Comparison full faithfulness and the specified evaluation squares transfer q naturality and the alpha isomorphism. All finite-Tor inputs have etale representatives, so these clauses hold on every piece and boundary. This gives exactly [def-weil-boundary-normalized-model], without using either beta conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_normalized_models
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (n : ℕ) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))
    [IsSeparated aY] [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY] :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian aY
    letI : CompactSpace Y := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace aY
    letI : IsNoetherian Y := ⟨⟩
    ∃ o : Operations Boundary
        (fun T : Piece Y ↦ FixedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) T.scheme)
        (fun T : Piece Y ↦ FixedEtaleCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) T.scheme),
      CanonicalOperations (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) Y aY
        (finiteComposition (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) Y aY) o ∧
      Nonempty (NormalizedModel o (fun T ↦ ctf l E n T.scheme))
